rows.witness: mx-strict-read-untracked-evt-apply-dispatch-shadow-named-signal-direct-none and fixtures/reactive-ir/event-dispatch-shadow/variants/shadow-creation-eval: a creation a JSX handler reaches, delivered into a shadow tree from an effect's apply, throws PRIMITIVE_IN_EFFECT_CALLBACK first (Chrome rc.21, runtime-oracle shadow-handler-forms); a shadow root attached by code built from a string is invisible to every scan
rows.why: ADR 1139 (bundle j smoke-census): App.tsx calls `eval`, so a shadow root and a dispatch from an effect's apply are both possible (the narrowing's fail-closed half, apply_dispatch_into_shadow_possible: eval or a code-evaluating call counts); the SC7002 row of a creation the handler may reach is creation-throws-first (uncertifiable), though this program attaches no shadow root (Chrome reports SYNC_NODE_RECEIVED_ASYNC). The other four of the six (lst-handler-object, export-namespace-call-handler) stay violations. Only the memo twin is an id of the proved ledger (proved/mx-census.json), so the row names it and the collateral is 1; its effect twin (...-flw-owned-eval-effect-direct-none) moves alike (the census manifest expects recall-gap for both) but was never a ledger entry.

rows.witness: mx-context-not-found-dny-flush-load-x-direct-none (and dny-flush-popover, dny-flush-unmount; fixtures/reactive-ir/context-read-owner-varies, Varies): Chrome rc.21 throws NO_OWNER_CONTEXT where main 960bfa1f9 reported missing-context-provider (SC4002, CONTEXT_NOT_FOUND) at a useContext in a JSX handler (onLoad, onBeforeToggle, onBlur) that a later flush reaches unowned (the census false positives of open-defects)
rows.why: ADR 1177 (bundle s, full census leg of the smoke): a context read written in a JSX handler whose owner varies by caller or may be null makes no provider claim (`owner-check-throws-first`: an unowned delivery may come first and throw NO_OWNER_CONTEXT). These 33 programs (context-not-found: dny-* 30, evt-* 2, pos-handler-owner 1) are the true proofs it withholds beside the three false positives: Chrome reports CONTEXT_NOT_FOUND at them because the owned run came first (a dispatch or an insertion at mount, e.g. dny-click-any, dny-load-show, dny-dispose-body), so the provider claim was right. One more program, mx-context-not-found-dny-change-checkbox-retyped-x-direct-none, moves alike and is in no ledger. Recovered when an order proof shows that a run at mount, before the handler can be delivered, is the first (docs/open-work.md, ADR 1177).
